item.title: [7.5] Bond turbulence means it’s time for the ECB to put QT on hold
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Eurozone inflation stands at 3.8%, with Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel warning of upside risks from energy, food and refining costs. However, wage and price-setting remain contained, while long-term inflation expectations stay aligned with the ECB’s 2% target. Markets increasingly expect further ECB rate hikes, though Nagel urged flexibility.

WHY IT MATTERS

The potential shift in ECB quantitative tightening amid bond market turbulence signals a material change in monetary policy dynamics for eurozone assets.

item.title: [7.2] Global Market: Eurozone business activity hits 29-month high as price pressure intensifies
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Eurozone business activity expanded at its fastest pace since April 2023 in September, driven by strong service demand and AI investments.
